;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**[[December 2019 Mogadishu bombing]]
***A [[Suicide attack|suicide]] [[Car bomb|truck bomb]]ing at a [[security checkpoint]] in [[Mogadishu]] kills at least 79 people and injures 149 others. No group has claimed responsibility. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/12/28/africa/somalia-unrest-bombing-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A [[Taliban]] attack on an [[Afghan National Army|Afghan military]] base in [[Sangin District]], [[Helmand Province]], kills at least 10 Afghan soldiers and injures 4 others. [https://www.voanews.com/south-central-asia/taliban-assault-army-base-kills-10-afghan-soldiers (VOA)]
*[[Monsey Hanukkah stabbing]]
**Five people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] at the home of a [[Hasidic Judaism|Hasidic]] [[rabbi]], during [[Hanukkah]] celebrations, in [[Monsey, New York]]. The suspect was later apprehended by [[New York City Police Department|the police]]. [[New York (state)|New York]] [[Governor of New York|governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] calls it an "act of [[domestic terrorism in the United States|domestic terrorism]]". [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/nypd-adl-monitoring-reports-of-stabbing-at-synagogue/2019/12/28/4eb05460-29f5-11ea-9cc9-e19cfbc87e51_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[North Korean ghost ships|North Korean ghost ship]] washes up on the shore of [[Japan]]'s [[Sado, Niigata|Sado Island]], containing the corpses of five people onboard, suspected to be fishermen. The bodies are described by [[Japanese police]] as "partially skeletonised", suggesting the boat has been adrift at sea for a long time. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-50934145 (BBC News)]
*Five people are killed when a plane crashes near a [[Walmart]] supermarket in [[Lafayette, Louisiana|Lafayette]], [[Louisiana]]. One occupant survives, while three others on the ground are injured. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-50935208 (BBC News)]
*[[Indonesia]]n [[palm oil]] tanker ship [[motor vessel|MV]] ''[[Namse Bangdzod]]'' vanishes in the [[Java Sea]]. The ship, with a crew of twelve, is theorised by rescuers to be the victim of [[piracy]], a notion dismissed by the [[indonesian Navy|Navy]]. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2019/01/10/the-curious-case-of-the-namse-bangdzod-mystery-shrouds-vessels-disappearance.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]
;Law and crime
*[[Corruption in Vietnam]]
**A court in [[Vietnam]] sentences former information minister Nguyen Bac Son to [[life in prison]] after finding him guilty of accepting $3 million in [[kickback (bribery)|kickbacks]] via an overpriced purchase of Audio Visual Global JSC for nearly 8.9 [[trillion]] [[Vietnamese dong|dong]] ($383.7 million) in late 2015 by [[Government of Vietnam|government]]-owned company [[MobiFone]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vietnam-corruption/vietnam-court-sentences-ex-minister-to-life-in-mobifone-corruption-scandal-idUSKBN1YW02M?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Prostitution in China]]
**The [[National People's Congress]] abolishes the use of [[unfree labour|forced labor]] to punish [[sex worker]]s, but states that [[prostitution]] will remain illegal. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-lawmaking-prostitution/china-scraps-extra-judicial-forced-labor-for-sex-workers-idUSKBN1YW08M?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Algerian protests]]
**[[Algeria]]n [[President of Algeria|President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] appoints former [[University of Algiers]] professor [[Abdelaziz Djerrad]] to be the new [[Prime Minister of Algeria|Prime Minister]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-algeria-politics/algeria-names-new-prime-minister-idUSKBN1YW08G?il=0 (Reuters)]
